q: The Amari-Nagaoka book (Methods of Information Geometry) shows that the maximum likelihood estimator θ̂_MLE is first-order efficient because it achieves:
opts: The Cramér-Rao bound asymptotically: √n(θ̂ − θ) →_d N(0, G(θ)^{-1})
Exact Fisher efficiency for all sample sizes
The same variance for all estimators
exp: MLE is first-order efficient: asymptotically it achieves the Cramér-Rao bound G(θ)^{-1}/n (where G(θ) is the Fisher information matrix). In information-geometric terms, MLE is the e-geodesic projection of the empirical distribution onto the model manifold.
